newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Chevron drills in remote Angolan oil field.
newsitem.headline: Chevron drills in remote Angolan oil field.

text.p: U.S.-based Chevron oil company has started production on a remote oil field off Angola's northern coast and is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels per day by year end, the company said on Tuesday.
The North N'Dola field, located in Area C on Block Zero, was discovered 25 years ago, but because of the remoteness of the field about 50 km (32 miles) off the Cabinda coast, it was not developed.
A number of fields have since been discovered in the same block much closer to shore.

Block Zero in total produces about 400,000 barrels per day and is operated by Chevron's subsidiary, the Cabinda Gulf Oil Company, with shareholders Angola's state oil company SONANGOL, Italy's Agip and France's Elf Aquitaine.
